newsitem.title: CHINA: China EximBank to boost loans to exporters 50 pct.
newsitem.headline: China EximBank to boost loans to exporters 50 pct.

text.p: The Export-Import Bank of China (EximBank) will increase loans to exporters of electronics and other capital goods by over 50 percent this year, a senior bank official said on Thursday.

EximBank's credits for exports this year were planned at 19.7 billion yuan and $101 million, up from an actual 12.8 billion yuan and $53 million last year, board chairman Tong Zhiguang said at the bank's annual meeting.

Export credits last year, which were 86.9 percent more than the previous year, financed $4.27 billion worth of electronics and machinery exports. Export of ships and large sets of electronic products rose 40 percent and 21 percent respectively, Xinhua news agency quoted him as saying.

EximBank reported considerable achievements in tapping the export credit insurance and guarantees field, Tong said, noting that business in the two items stood at $610 million and $320 million dollars, respectively.
The bank had approved restructuring of overseas government loans for 53 projects last year, with the contractual value reaching $1.8 billion, he said.
Outstanding foreign government loans of the EximBank totaled $15.53 billion by the end of last year, more than half the total of such loans to China.
